findings.body: `git diff HEAD` compares the working tree with HEAD, so staged and unstaged changes can cancel out. For example, edit README.md, stage it, then restore its working-tree contents to HEAD without unstaging. This check returns nothing despite the pending staged change, allowing the fix and installation to proceed. Item 1 requires refusal before creating anything whenever tracked files have uncommitted changes. Use a tracked-only status check that examines both the index and working tree, and cover this case. See the [Git diff contract](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff).
findings.title: Not done: refuse all uncommitted changes to tracked files

findings.body: The required leftover-folder case checks the file's bytes only if the file still exists. If the command deleted draft.txt while refusing, this assertion would be skipped and the case would pass: its snapshot observes refs, worktree registrations, uv calls and PR calls, but not file contents. Item 1 explicitly requires this test to prove that the leftover file remains unchanged. Make the byte assertion unconditional for that case so deletion also fails the test.
findings.title: Not done: leftover-folder refusal preserves the file's bytes

findings.body: A resumed upgrade fix containing a staged rename produces a porcelain record such as `R  new.txt\0old.txt\0`. Splitting on NUL and slicing every entry by three characters returns `new.txt` and `.txt`, corrupting the source filename. Upgrade passes these paths into `repo.commit_state`, whose `git add` at src/forge/repo.py:468 fails on the nonexistent truncated path, preventing the rerun from committing and closing. Disable rename detection for this listing or parse rename records explicitly. The [Git status contract](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-status) documents the separate source-filename field.
findings.title: Parse both filenames in staged rename records
